title: Kenyan Chips Masala
community: Popular across urban Kenya — a beloved street food
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Chips Masala — crispy deep-fried chips tossed immediately after frying in a fragrant spice mix of curry powder, paprika, cumin, chilli, and salt. The most beloved street food upgrade in Kenya — transforming plain chips into something bold, addictive, and completely Kenyan.
longDesc: Chips masala is the Kenyan genius of taking something good — crispy fried chips — and making it extraordinary with a simple spice blend applied at the moment they come out of the fryer. The heat of the freshly fried chips helps the spices bloom and adhere. Every bite delivers crunch, heat, and fragrance. At every Kenyan food stall, the question is not 'chips or masala chips' — it is just masala chips.
ingredients: 800g potatoes — peeled and cut into thick chips

substitutions.alternative: Frozen chips — fry from frozen at 180°C
Cayenne pepper or omit for mild version

steps: Peel and cut potatoes into thick chips. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes — this removes excess starch for crispier chips.
Drain and dry the chips thoroughly — water causes dangerous oil splatter.
Mix all spices and salt together in a large bowl. Set aside.
Fry chips in batches for 5—7 minutes until golden and crispy. Do not overcrowd.
Remove immediately from the oil and drain briefly.
While still piping hot, toss the chips in the spice mix bowl. Coat thoroughly.
Add fresh coriander and lemon juice if using. Toss once more.
chefTips: The spice mix must go on immediately after frying — the heat of the chips is what makes the spices bloom and adhere.
Soaking chips in cold water before frying makes them significantly crispier.
Dry the chips completely before frying — moisture makes them soggy and causes dangerous oil splatter.
commonMistakes: Adding spices to cold chips — they do not bloom or stick properly.
Wet chips in the fryer — splatter and soggy result.
Overcrowding the fryer — lowers temperature and produces oily chips.

faqs.q: Can I use an air fryer?
faqs.a: Yes — air fry at 200°C for 18—20 minutes, shaking halfway. Toss in the spice mix immediately when they come out of the air fryer while still hot.

cookingScience: The high surface temperature of freshly fried chips (around 150—160°C) instantly volatilises the aromatic compounds in the spice mix, creating the characteristic fragrant bloom. At room temperature, these compounds would not volatilise and the spices would taste flat and raw.
sustainabilityTips: Buy local Kenyan potatoes — supporting smallholder farmers.
storage: Best eaten immediately — chips lose crispiness rapidly.
reheating: Not recommended — reheat in oven at 200°C for 5 minutes if necessary.
healthBenefits: Potatoes provide potassium and vitamin C.
Best enjoyed as an occasional treat.
culturalNote: Chips masala is arguably the most universally loved Kenyan street food — found at every kiosk, food stall, and roadside restaurant across the country. The simple genius of tossing hot chips in a fragrant spice mix has made it one of the defining flavours of Kenyan urban street food culture.
regionalVariations: Chips masala with kachumbari on top.
